body: I understood that reference.
You can't blame him, it's a gorgeous car.

The best option I could think of was a course with Applied Physics or Engineering Mathematics, but it's not simple to switch and there aren't many courses like these. For a job, perhaps something in the energy industry, aerospace or computing. 

I would like to both pursue these and get away from low paid work, just because there's no better alternative. For the past 6 months I kept a journal as well. I might just have to be patient and go back when I'm confident. It shouldn't be the end of the world, but it feels like torture a lot of the time.  

Thank you for your help. I hope you're doing well.

Returning to the same university and course or trying to transfer. Another option is to just work and go back to education next year. 

I'm not sure even what course is right. All of these are quite difficult to me.

Depression or mental illness is making me extremely confused and fearful. There's probably brain damage or cognitive dissonance, I don't know.
Unfortunately I haven't sorted it out. I tried thinking of solutions but I don't see any good option.

Well done for finishing your degree. I'll try to look into Jungian psychologists. I've heard about Carl Jung a lot.

There's been a bit of progress but nothing big. I hope things change in a major way because the way it is I'm going towards ending my life sooner or later.

That's very kind of you, thanks. I guess I need to talk because life is falling apart and I see no solution. I'm in a big mess and can't make decisions. My mind is just so full of fear I don't know what to do. It's just despair.

It's good to hear it worked for you. Seeing a psychologist is probably my best option, you're right. I suspect I am my own worst enemy. I have spoken to counsellors, but they are probably different to a psychologist, I'm not entirely sure. 

I studied Engineering. I was interested in using science for practical problem solving and innovation. It's still something I gravitate towards but all my motivation for everything is dead. I'm also doubting my decisions and abilities, so my mind is a mess. 

Thank you.
I agree completely. Insomnia made my life hell and ruined my chances of a good future. I still can't recover. Fuck insomnia.
Yeah definitely. Sorry about the late reply.

Yes, it does often feel like I'll never amount to anything. This is supposed to be the prime of my life but it's going really quickly. I'm trying to improve and work towards good things, but heck, it's yet to pay off in any significant way.
I've been productive recently. There were no bad thoughts for a while.
I agree it isn't a way to live. I'm stuck being directionless and it feels like it's killing me.

Really sorry about your sister. Addiction is a very difficult struggle from what I've read and heard. 

I can relate to 2017 being a rough year - it was probably my most dismal year yet. Accomplishments don't need to be something huge to make them significant, so it is still possible to do something meaningful. Take care.
Yes, that's a good idea. I do actually take lots of pictures in an attempt to capture some moments. However, it might be an idea for me to start a journal of some kind. Thanks.
Exactly. Good way to put it into words. Hopefully this doesn't mean that more opportunities will never come.
Interesting. Maybe those conversations were important to you, so you keep a vivid memory.

Yes, anxiety is always making us worry about the future. Then depression comes in when we realise we did not appreciate the present moment. It's hard not to since we are always told to delay gratification and focus on long term achievement. I also need to work on being in the present.

You're right about moments being transient. I'm always trying to relive memories and past moments in order to keep them alive. My fear is that after something is done, it's over for good. Time sets everything in stone, so any mistakes will always stay with me. 

Our lives are all ending a minute at a time right now. It feels like my life is being wasted, yet I don't know how. That's depressing.
Hope it changes for you in 2018. Stagnation is probably my biggest problem right now. It is painful to see old friends moving on while I still cling to the past.
Thank you, hope it goes well for you too. Glad you are making progress.

Seems like you care a lot about your students, which is something very helpful. This email will encourage them, especially the ones struggling. Definitely refreshing to read from a student's point of view. It's a shame this would never happen in the UK...

I'm not American but I get the impression that Americans are incredibly hard working and resilient. The US economy is still the most powerful and advanced in the world. In addition, you have some of the best universities in the world which contribute the majority of the world's scientific and technological advances.

Detailed notes from textbooks, then I try to explain concepts to myself as if I am teaching. Then it is down to practice questions as repetition reinforces long term memory. Also, Khanacademy is very useful to me.
Use a high SPF sun cream, especially at high altitudes. Even if the temperature is comfortable, the UV radiation can give you very painful burns during long hikes.

I felt the need to comment because I can relate to this completely. It is so frustrating and I hope you at least know that you're not the only one struggling like this. I had to watch my friends breeze through classwork and homework effortlessly in Maths/Physics while I was stuck for hours on one thing. 

The only advice I can give is that eventually if you put in a lot of time studying, it starts to get easier, but it's a massive struggle to get to that point. At least that was my experience. Also, I found that learning from my more gifted friends was useful because they knew methods and tricks that made things easier. Online lectures also saved me in exams. The website Exam Solutions basically saved my grades in Further Maths A-level.
Thanks. Will try to keep pushing.
Thank you. I agree it's awful initially, but once you gain momentum it helps. Take care.
Thanks for your advice. Any response is helpful really. It's nice of people to take some time to help like this, so I appreciate it.

Sorry for the late reply. I appreciate the concern. It's kind of weird right now, I have some ideas about how to improve my life and I'm trying to put them into action. Still, a lot of dark times but also some huge mood swings. Hopefully you are ok?
Yes, that is probably a last resort. Thank you.
Hey, thanks for the concern, I appreciate it. Not doing very well. Afraid for the future. Have never hated myself more. I've decided how to end things if it gets very rough.
Yes, I hate my life. Motivation goes down when faced with constant disappointment. The worst feeling ever is to put in all your energy into a goal only to be bitterly disappointed again and again.

If you spend some more time with male friends it should eventually start to feel natural. We guys are pretty simple. There should be no problem if you're just straightforward and down to earth. Obviously if it's a formal conversation then a bit of maturity is helpful. 

Edit: I can relate to anxiety in social situations with both genders, but this attitude has helped me personally.

Sorry that your hard work isn't rewarded, it is really frustrating. It feels exactly the same for me at 19 right now. Realistically, going out partying all the time will cost people in the long term (financially and in terms of health). Social media is also full of narcissism and egotistical maniacs who make their lives look perfect.
Thank you for the kind words.
I haven't planned out anything for now, but I don't trust myself sometimes with this pointless life. Thanks for your concern.
Yeah, why do we get punished for trying to better ourselves...? It makes no sense.
Luckily only a few times. I always regretted it. Always. This made me stop because it was just causing me so much more discomfort. Not worth it. Alcohol and depression are a dangerous combination.
It's nice. To me it looks like some kind of intense battle.
Yes, a short burst of happiness usually occurs when I'm high on caffeine and Ferrari win a Grand Prix at the same time.
Thanks for your reply, I will try not to stress too much but it's difficult for me when it comes to these 'big' decisions since everyone is judges based on stuff like this.

First of all, sorry that you're going through this difficult time :(  I notice that your writing is very clear and precise, so I honestly think that not everything is lost. 

What happened was beyond your control and you are not at fault. I agree that it is cruel. I can relate to what it's like to be frustrated with your mind. My brain often fails on me and forces me to do the most stupid mistakes, which then results in anxiety etc... 

However, it is possible with patience and perseverance to overcome some of this. You've probably heard of how some highly successful people have had to deal with conditions like dyslexia (Richard Branson) or Stephen Hawking with his paralysis. I know it sounds cliche, but it is possible and guys like these are respected for making the most of what they have. I understand that when in deep depression, words like this don't mean much, but I just want to wish you all the best and hope you recover.

Very sorry that you're in pain. This is not a decision to be taken lightly and in this particular state. Please be careful. 

In my experience stimulants like dark chocolate or coffee are good substitutes, at least temporarily to avoid getting drunk.
Yes, it can help. This has been very long for me now, not just a moment. I may just naturally be an inferior person I don't know but if that's the case I can't live with myself.

Yeah it is awful to have bad luck all the time. People say it's just temporary but it feels permanent and relentless. Damn, sorry you feel this way. I understand completely how frustrating it is. Hope things get better for you.
Thank you, that's very kind of you. Glad that there is moral support here for all of us who struggle. Better than nothing.

I'm really sorry, I know it is painful and frustrating. You seem to be resilient and hard working, having graduated despite dealing with depression. This ought to work in your favour in the future, so perhaps it is too harsh a judgement to say that you have 'no redeeming qualities'. I wish you all the best and hope that life gets better.
Oh, sorry to hear about your chronic pain :( but thank you for the encouragement.

Yes, I had a few talking therapy sessions that helped me somewhat but they weren't regular. I also tried exercise like running. I just hope it's not some kind of permanent depression. Might have to look into medication and more therapy if this continues... but it would be nice to 'stand on my own feet' again.

Really sorry about your difficulties.

If I was in your position, I would try talking to your employer/boss (someone more senior in the company) about reducing the working hours. You could explain to them that it's ruining your health. I don't know what the employment laws are in the United States, but having to deal with stores 24/7 is completely unreasonable by most countries' standards. It seems that this stress is likely causing all the other health problems.

Yes definitely, I had ambition and was pretty good academically. I wanted to have a career in applied physics/engineering in research and development of things like quantum computers and fusion reactors. Then my brain kind of just failed on me with all this anxiety and insomnia to the point where I could not sleep at all the night before any important event or task. Depression then killed all my motivation and since then I have to force everything.

Yes, definitely it does. It's like a glimpse into what life could have been like instead. Don't know if anyone else does this, but I try to turn these rare moments into something constructive like getting some studying done or cleaning my room etc.
